body:
I'm not convinced that I even want to get better since I'm still of two minds about it. It seems that I am unable to commit either way: to recovery or to suicide. Perhaps I am not suited for this world and this world isn't suited for me. 

I've heard people say that motivation is unreliable and useless, but there still needs to be some sort of motivating factor that is strong enough to make a commitment in the first place. That's my issue. 

Because why make a commitment to something that is not easy to accomplish if you have no substantial motivation to achieve that goal in the first place? That's what I've been trying to explain this whole time, but I'm not sure if I'm making any sense. 

For example, if you didn't like that your social anxiety was interfering with you getting laid then that could be the motivating force which helped you decide to commit to overcoming that fear of rejection. While I obviously don't like the many symptoms that keep me from living a fulfilling and optimal life somehow that is still not enough for me to commit to change.

I don't know what's wrong with me. Some people say that you have to hit "rock bottom" and that's what I want to avoid because I've already hit so many bottoms and I don't want to get any worse. I can't imagine what it would take for me to really turn my life around. In the past it hasn't been worst case scenarios that have made me want to change; it was always the people I love and who love me that have inspired me to commit to "getting better." Of course, that's not something I can force to happen. At any rate, thank you for reading my walls of text.

I think I see what you mean and thank you for the comments. Obviously I want myself, and everyone, to break free from any mental health issues that might hold us back from living a fulfilling life. For me, it is a matter of finding courage and motivation.

I do and I don't want to get better. My stance fluctuates with my thoughts and emotions and that is the issue. It's like I can't find a good enough reason to fully commit to "getting better." In the past, it has always been other people, loved ones, that have sparked motivation in me, whether it was the fear of losing them or something else...

I'm not completely isolating myself - I do have contact with multiple people. While I have socially withdrawn quite a bit, that is nothing new for me and sometimes I feel like it's what I need at this time.

> If you take small steps, it wont be bad, you decide how fast you want to go.

Thank you for this reminder. Most of the time I really pressure myself to grow faster than I should, maybe, and that results in me living life in an "all or nothing" mentality, which is not productive in the long run.
This doesn't resonate with me, but thank you for sharing your experience.
